title: Online ticketing is becoming a cultural-access gateway in Europe, but digital purchase rates remain sharply place-stratified
source_unit: Eurostat, EU survey on the use of ICT in households and by individuals: online event-ticket purchases in 2025
geography: European Union; individuals across EU Member States purchasing tickets online for cultural or other events

denominator.unit: EU individuals covered by the ICT household and individual survey; source article reports shares without pooled respondent count

online_event_ticket_purchase_2025.unit: percent of EU individuals purchasing event tickets online in the previous three months

online_event_ticket_purchase_2024_derive.unit: percent of EU individuals; derived from 2025 share minus reported 3.8-point increase

mechanism.value: Digital ticketing is converting online access into a direct cultural-consumption gateway, reducing some transaction friction while making device access, payment, identity, and platform availability part of event participation

observations.method: Eurostat EU ICT household and individual survey indicator for online purchases of tickets to events during the previous three months.
observations.uncertainty: The measure captures a recent purchase, not attendance, ticket price, event type, repeat participation, resale, household income, or whether online access expanded or merely displaced in-person purchasing.
observations.subgroup: EU individuals covered by the ICT household and individual survey; event tickets include cultural or other events according to the source indicator.
observations.counterinterpretation: The increase may reflect temporary event calendars, post-pandemic normalization, price or supply changes, or more online payment use without broader cultural participation.

denominator.unit: EU Member State individuals covered by the ICT household and individual survey; source article reports country shares without pooled respondent count

ireland_online_ticket_purchase.unit: percent of individuals in Ireland purchasing event tickets online in the previous three months

netherlands_online_ticket_purchase.unit: percent of individuals in the Netherlands purchasing event tickets online in the previous three months

denmark_online_ticket_purchase.unit: percent of individuals in Denmark purchasing event tickets online in the previous three months

bulgaria_online_ticket_purchase.unit: percent of individuals in Bulgaria purchasing event tickets online in the previous three months

romania_online_ticket_purchase.unit: percent of individuals in Romania purchasing event tickets online in the previous three months

italy_online_ticket_purchase.unit: percent of individuals in Italy purchasing event tickets online in the previous three months

high_low_country_gap.unit: percentage-point difference between Ireland and Bulgaria

mechanism.value: Online cultural-consumption infrastructure is not evenly realized across Europe: country-level payment, platform, income, event-supply, and participation ecologies determine whether digital ticketing becomes a normal access route

observations.method: Eurostat country comparison from the same 2025 ICT household and individual survey indicator.
observations.uncertainty: Country differences are descriptive and do not identify the contribution of income, payment systems, broadband, event supply, cultural habits, age structure, or survey response patterns.
observations.subgroup: Individuals in EU Member States, with country estimates reported by Eurostat.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower online ticket purchase may reflect more cash or in-person purchasing, different event markets, fewer desired events, or different survey interpretation rather than lower cultural participation.

denominator.unit: Eurostat culture-statistics ICT indicator availability frame

cultural_ticket_measure.value: online purchases of tickets to cultural or other events

measurement_boundary.value: purchase is observed before attendance, experience, repeat use, and cultural meaning

mechanism.value: Digital transaction data can reveal an early conversion stage between interest and cultural attendance, allowing the program to separate demand, payment access, ticket acquisition, and realized participation

observations.method: Eurostat culture-statistics and ICT-purchase indicator framing, with the online ticket purchase measure treated as a pre-attendance conversion stage.
observations.uncertainty: The source does not identify event category, transaction value, seller, attendance realization, resale, accessibility, or whether purchasing was for the respondent or someone else.
observations.subgroup: EU individuals participating in the ICT household and individual survey.
observations.counterinterpretation: A purchase can be a one-off or unsuccessful transaction; online ticketing may widen access for some users while excluding people without suitable devices, payment methods, or confidence.

related_sources.claim: Eurostat's source dataset provides the underlying online purchasing indicators for event tickets and other culture-related goods and services.
The Guide to Eurostat culture statistics documents the culture-related ICT purchase variables and their coverage across years.

boundary: This record adds EU evidence on online event-ticket purchasing, growth, country variation, and the pre-attendance conversion stage in cultural consumption. It does not measure attendance, event quality, ticket prices, household affordability, cultural meaning, payment exclusion, or causal effects of digital ticketing.
